text:
Chandler Stephenson has two Stanley Cup rings and 13 points in 21 games, 11 of them assists. Read only the box score and he looks like the playmaking centre Seattle signed. The underlying numbers tell a harder story.

At five on five, the Kraken get 39% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 8.8 points worse than when he sits. He has 17 shots in 21 games, and his own chances are thin. He's also pointless in five straight, though the chances around him have been there in that stretch (3.3 expected goals), and Seattle has scored 8.6 fewer goals than it deserved with him on the ice. That luck usually swings back, so expect a few more points. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) says his offense lives in transition, 56% of his shots off the rush. Evolving-Hockey had him below replacement last season. Our range projects 40 to 60 points. The question for Seattle is whether he keeps a top-six role as the young centres push.
